The Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY) Movement, Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD), ALAB, and other patriotic organizations denounced the violent use of water cannons and the continued harassment of Filipino fishermen by Chinese vessels in Escoda Shoal, an area well within the Philippines’ Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

The groups said these actions violate Philippine sovereignty and endanger the lives, safety, and livelihoods of local fishermen, noting that water cannons can cause injuries and damage fishing boats.

Members of the groups held a protest outside the Chinese Consulate Office along Gil Puyat Avenue in Makati City on December 16. (Contributed Photos)

🚨🇦🇺 BONDI BEACH TERROR SUSPECTS VISITED SOUTHERN PHILIPPINES WEEKS BEFORE ATTACK, PROMPTING PROBE INTO POSSIBLE MILITANT LINKS

Australian and Philippine authorities are probing a nearly month-long trip to the Philippines made by the father-and-son suspects in the deadly Bondi Beach terror attack, just weeks before the December 14 shooting that killed 15 people at a Hanukkah celebration.

NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon confirmed that Sajid Akram (50, the father, killed at the scene) and Naveed Akram (24, the son, critically injured and in custody) traveled there last month.

According to the Philippine Bureau of Immigration:

- Sajid Akram (Indian national) and Naveed Akram (Australian citizen) arrived in the Philippines on November 1 from Sydney.
- Their declared destination was Davao, a key city in the southern Philippines region historically associated with Islamist militant groups, including Abu Sayyaf and ISIS-affiliated elements.
- They departed on November 28, returning to Sydney via Manila.

Philippine National Police are verifying details and investigating the pair's activities during their stay. Security sources have indicated the duo may have received military-style training in the area.

Australian investigators are examining the purpose of the trip, potential contacts, and any ties to extremist networks.

The attack, declared an act of terrorism motivated by Islamic State ideology, saw the gunmen open fire on a crowd of Jewish families and celebrants at Bondi Beach.

Sources: ABC News, The Guardian, BBC, Reuters, The New York Times, Sky News
